sentences.text: The appellant is the claimant in the claim petition in MVC No.213/2017 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Shorapur [for short, 'the Tribunal'].

The Tribunal, by the judgment and award dated 14.03.2018, has granted to the appellant, who was aged 12 years as of the date of the road accident [29.01.2017], a total NC: 2024:KHC-K:625-DB sum of Rs.11,45,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of his claim petition.

The Tribunal has awarded the aforesaid amount under the following heads:
 Description Amount  Loss of future income due to Rs.5,00,000.00  disability  Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000.00  Loss of amenities Rs.1,00,000.00

Rounded of Rs.11,45,000.00 2.

There is no dispute that the appellant, as a consequence of the injuries suffered, has suffered amputation of his left lower limb below knee and that the Insurer, who had insured the offending vehicle viz., the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-33/TA-2509 during the relevant period, is liable to pay to the appellant just and reasonable compensation to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle.
The appellant seeks enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

Sri Babu H.
Metagudda, the learned counsel for the appellant, is heard in the light of these circumstances.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards loss of future income because of permanent disability relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another1.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, Sri Babu H.
Metagudda proposes to rely upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kajal V/s Jagdish Chand and Others2 to contend that in certain circumstances it would be permissible to grant compensation towards loss of future income to a minor based on the notified minimum wages adding appropriate percentage thereof towards future prospects with necessary capitalization applying the appropriate multiplier and after deduction towards personal expenses.

entities.text: Kajal V/s Jagdish Chand and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. This Court must observe that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kajal vs. Jagadish Chand [supra] has observed that each case must be decided on its own evidence while examining the question of just and 1 2014 (14) SCC 396 2 (2020) 4 SCC 413 NC: 2024:KHC-K:625-DB reasonable compensation in a case where a minor was rendered paraplegic because of the injuries suffered in the road accident.

In the present case, the appellant has suffered amputation of left lower limb below knee and though this injury is a crippling injury, it cannot be said that his earning capability is completely diminished as in the case of a person who is rendered paraplegic.

5. This Court, therefore, is of the considered view that compensation must be awarded in terms of the position in Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited [supra].

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctor has assessed permanent disability at 80% and in that event the appellant would be entitled for the upper limit as observed by the Tribunal, but there must be necessary enhancement given the lapse of time between the date of accident in Master Mallikarjun [supra] and in the present case.

The accident in the present case is of the year 2017 and this Court is of the considered view that the just compensation would be in a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- as against the sum of NC: 2024:KHC-K:625-DB Rs.5,00,000/- as awarded in the case of Master Mallikarjun where the accident is in the year 2006.

6. Sri Babu H. Metagudda next submits that there must be just and reasonable compensation towards [a] pain and suffering, [b] loss of amenities, [c] loss of marriage prospects, [d] the cost of Askash vs Tippanna Naik And Anr on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110455670/
3 acquiring artificial limb and replacement thereof over decades that the appellant will have to live and [e] appropriate addition towards conveyance and attendant charges during the laid-up period.

entities.text: Askash vs Tippanna Naik And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- each towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities.
The appellant has suffered amputation after hospitalization.

This Court is of the considered view, for the purposes of awarding just and reasonable compensation which will not be a bonanza, that a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- must be awarded towards pain and suffering as against the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities but in the present case given the age of the appellant, this Court is of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:625-DB considered view that a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- would be just and reasonable compensation.
There must be appropriate compensation towards loss of marriage prospects inasmuch as it is certain that the appellant's marriage prospects are vastly undermined with his amputation.

Sri Babu H. Metagudda submits that there must be a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under this head, but in the facts and circumstances of the case this Court is of the considered view that a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- would be just and reasonable.
8. The Tribunal has not granted any sum towards the cost of artificial limb and replacement thereof.
The appellant will not only have to buy artificial limb but also keep replacing it over the decades because he is young.
This Court, in view of the yardstick that is employed in this regard, is of the considered view that a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- would be just and reasonable.
The Tribunal has granted a total sum of Rs.17,600/- towards attendant and conveyance charges for the laid-up period.
The appellant was inpatient NC: 2024:KHC-K:625-DB for a period of 44 days and must have been confined to bed further.
It would therefore be appropriate to award such amount which would be just and reasonable under these two heads.
A total sum of Rs.50,000/- would be just and reasonable.

9. In the light of the above, the computation of just and reasonable compensation and enhancement in the compensation would be as follows:

Medical expenses Rs.4,27,511.00 Rs.4,27,511.00 Loss of marriage - Rs.2,00,000.00
prospects

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is partly allowed.
